mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about glucagon is TRUE?

options.A: Glucagon promotes the synthesis of glycogen in the liver.
options.B: Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, raising blood glucose.
options.C: Glucagon is secreted by beta cells of the islets of Langerhans.
options.D: Glucagon lowers blood glucose by enhancing cellular uptake of glucose.

mcqs.answer: Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, raising blood glucose.
mcqs.explanation: Glucagon, released from alpha cells of the islets, raises blood glucose by stimulating glycogen breakdown (glycogenolysis) and new glucose formation (gluconeogenesis) in the liver. Option A describes insulin action, Option C misidentifies the secreting cell type, and Option D describes the opposite effect of glucagon.

mcqs.question: The islets of Langerhans contain several cell types. If a researcher isolates only the peripheral region of an islet, which hormone is most likely to be abundant in the extract and why?

options.A: Insulin, because beta cells are uniformly distributed throughout the islet.
options.B: Glucagon, because alpha cells are predominantly located at the periphery of the islet.
options.C: Somatostatin, because delta cells form a central core in the islet.
options.D: Pancreatic polypeptide, because PP cells are only found in the central region.

mcqs.answer: Glucagon, because alpha cells are predominantly located at the periphery of the islet.
mcqs.explanation: Alpha cells, which secrete glucagon, are mainly situated at the outer rim of the islets, whereas beta cells (insulin) are concentrated centrally. Therefore a peripheral isolate will be rich in glucagon. Options A, C, and D misrepresent the typical cellular distribution within the islet.

mcqs.question: Which pair of statements correctly compares the roles of insulin and glucagon in maintaining blood glucose homeostasis?

options.A: Insulin promotes glycogenolysis in liver, whereas glucagon stimulates glycogen synthesis in muscle.
options.B: Both insulin and glucagon increase glucose uptake by peripheral tissues during fasting.
options.C: Insulin lowers blood glucose by stimulating glucose uptake and glycogen synthesis; glucagon raises blood glucose by stimulating glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
options.D: Insulin and glucagon are secreted in response to high blood glucose levels.

mcqs.answer: Insulin lowers blood glucose by stimulating glucose uptake and glycogen synthesis; glucagon raises blood glucose by stimulating glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
mcqs.explanation: Insulin, released from beta cells, drives glucose into cells and promotes glycogen storage, thereby lowering blood glucose. Glucagon, from alpha cells, does the opposite: it triggers glycogen breakdown and new glucose production, raising blood glucose. Options A, B, and D describe actions that are opposite to the physiological reality.

mcqs.question: According to the diagnostic criteria of the International Diabetes Federation, which of the following plasma glucose values is sufficient to diagnose diabetes mellitus in an asymptomatic adult?

options.B: 2‑hour plasma glucose after 75 g oral glucose tolerance test = 180 mg/dL
options.C: Random plasma glucose = 190 mg/dL with classic symptoms of polyuria and polydipsia

mcqs.explanation: For an asymptomatic individual, diabetes can be diagnosed if any one of the following is met: fasting plasma glucose ≥126 mg/dL, 2‑hour OGTT glucose ≥200 mg/dL, HbA1c ≥6.5 %, or random plasma glucose ≥200 mg/dL with symptoms. Option D meets the criterion (HbA1c ≥6.5 %). Options A and B are below the diagnostic thresholds, and Option C, although high, requires the presence of symptoms, which the question states are absent.
